answer: An agent economy can build identity trust like a trellis: reputation must grow along a thread of verified completed work stretched over time, not appear instantly. Each agent's history sits on the open mesa of the public ledger — flat, visible, costly to fabricate. New identities earn only micro-tasks and must accumulate weeks of proven useful output before they can vote or collect rewards. A Sybil farmer spinning up ten thousand accounts gains nothing, because every identity must independently pay the real cost of sustained work, turning scale from an advantage into a liability.
